author: Crinos
body:
The Primordial patron is literally just an update of the 2014 genie Warlock. 
Not that I'm complaining mind you. 
I do like the path of lament Barbarians flavor (Linkin Park intensifies) and I like the Venom Monk (Five deadly venom's for the win!)

author: Fedifensor
body: Addressing the possible panic from those that like the Genie Warlock as is, this is a dark mirror of the Genie Warlock that has a different name and different abilities. It is not an update to Genie Warlock, literally or otherwise.

author: Crinos
body:
Yeah I may have jumped the gun on that assessment. There are some major differences. 
Firstly you don't get a genies vessel, instead you can create a "Node", a five foot space of power that you can hang out in and it gives you mechanical benefits. 
Also the spell selection of bonus elemental spells is much better, although they don't get the wish spell. Also the Primordial warlock gets resistance to their element later than the Genie Lock (Level 10 instead of level 6) with the benefit that it becomes full on immunity in the node. 
There are other differences too. Sorry for the confusion, my bad.

author: Kurotowa
body:
Venom Monk sidesteps the "so many enemies are Resistant or Immune to Poison damage" problem by letting you swap to dealing Acid damage. Cute solution, I suppose. I do like that the 6th level Toxic Touch has non-combat applications too.
...is Primordial Warlock supposed to be a backdoor Blade Pact enabler? It creates a repositionable zone that deals damage and gives the Warlock a hefty AC boost. That's better for Blade Pact than a lot of Warlock subclasses are.

author: La Marche Futilé
body:
My thoughts:
Lament Barbarian
A per-long rest ability with uses equal to con mod? That gives the enemy a con save to dodge it? And that does damage which essentially doesn't scale up at all? And that's the only level 3 feature they get? Hard pass, that is incredible garbage. Even being able to get the uses back by burning a rage use is no real consolation, since that's actually a resource that barbarians actually have to work to manage most adventuring days.
Getting Speak With Dead as a ritual at 6th is nice, that's a great utility spell in most games. And Frightening enemies on a hit is actually pretty good. Resistance to cold and necrotic later on is likewise fairly decent, although it's coming pretty late in your adventuring career. Seems like too little, too late in a class that is notorious for not being good to go deep into.
Although, as a fun thought, applying Frightened just requires a strength-based attack, not a melee attack, so you can potentially do it using a thrown weapon. Sadly, nothing else in the build synergizes well with that.
Venom Monk
Hmm. the toxin abilities seem pretty okay- surprisingly, there's no save involved and they both work just fine on creatures that are immune to poison/poisoned. Slowing Toxin is a pretty solid debuff, especially given how mobile the monk class is by default, and Venom allows you to frontload quite a bit of damage. Also you can make all poison damage acid damage, which is strange but pretty good because very few things have resistance/immunity to acid.
The level 6 stuff is kinda middling, but does give you something to do outside of combat scenes- there's some nice infiltration and social tech here, assuming they fail the save (and nothing stops you from just re-applying it if they do.) Being able to eat/absorb poison is a cute trick, although I don't think it actually will do a lot. But immunity to poison damage is certainly nice, as quite a lot of monsters do it. Retal damage on being his is likewise merely okay, since as a monk you really don't have the HP to spare to take a bunch of hits from people.The Hallucinogenic Breath is pretty much exactly the same as the Fear spell, except not AoE. That's probably... fine, I guess? If you can get them to consistently fail the save it's devastating, as you can potentially grapple them and then fear breath and they are completely stunlocked for the next minute. But there are a lot of things immune to frightened at that level, so it won't be as applicable as you might like. Still, a very strong trick when it works.
Primordial Warlock
Themed a lot like the Genie, but functionally completely different. The elemental node is... not terribly exciting. It's mostly fine as an AoE way to clear little guys, but warlock was not exactly hurting for AoE clearing spells- Flaming Sphere, Hunger of Hadar, Fireball, Sickening Radiance, Insect Plague, etc, all fill the role more than adequately. There's some decent spells in the bonus list, but nothing incredible. Although, being able to toss down 2-3 Walls of Stone per short rest does make the warlock potentially the most incredible builder ever, able to turn flat ground into a heavy fortification in the course of an afternoon.
The upgrade to the node that adds Charisma to your AC is kinda wild, especially since nothing stops you from wearing medium or heavy armor to go with it- dip one level of Fighter or Artificer and you're off to the races. Teleporting to the node is a little bit niche, but given that there's no actual range limit on the node and you don't need line of sight, it seems ripe for shenanigans. Send your node drifting across a huge chasm or up the side of a cliff, then teleport directly to it. Leave your node at the start of a dungeon, scout around, and teleport back when things get hairy. There's a lot that can be done there.
Resistance/immunity to the damage type is likewise a pretty neat feature, lots of possibilities there (although mostly outside your control, since the GM will pick traps and environments- fire and cold will come up a lot, though, and swimming through an acid lake to surprise someone is a cute thought.) I also like the type-changing invocation they added, as it makes theming your spells a lot easier. Sadly you don't get any kind of damage bonus the way Dragon Sorcerers do, so it's more narrative than impactful.

author: AJDynon
body: It's save for half damage, not save for no damage. And it's tied to your Con score, which they'll want to increase anyway, so it "stealth scales", I guess.

author: La Marche Futilé
body:
Possibly so, although that's actually a pretty inefficient way to use them, since poisons aren't generally cheap and the damage you gain is less than the damage the poison itself would do. Even with the ability to make them yourself, poisons aren't free.
They do save for half, but the damage is so low it barely matters past the initial levels and you don't get either of the rider effects on a successful save. You're doing 2d12 up until 9th level, and at that point monster HP has scaled up tremendously whereas you have added... +1 to your save difficulty, in all likelihood. It's the same crappy scaling problem that the Hell Knight suffered from- an ability that is vaguely fine at the level you get it, but quickly becomes useless as monster HP rises and your damage does not by an appreciable amount.

author: Manitou
body: Drinking poison also heals you. Not for much, but every bit counts. And it gives you more than one reason to drink it.

author: Morty
body: It seems pretty in line with barbarian subclasses historically, honestly. Maybe it's because the class is so laser-focused on rage that adding any other sources of combat performance is seen as excessive.

author: La Marche Futilé
body:
If so it's a pretty misguided philosophy, as barbarian has never been a top-tier damage class in 5e. Even without bringing significant optimization into play, it gets beaten by fighter, paladin, ranger, and warlock in tier 1/2 play pretty easily.
Giving a martial an AoE attack is nice, but having fewer uses than spellcasters will have max-level spell slots at that point is devastatingly weak. You're gonna feel real proud for 1-2 levels when that 2d12 damage feels very impressive and you evaporate some goblin hordes with it and then it will drop off extremely quickly.

author: Morty
body: Well, yeah, I didn't say it makes any sense. But it's also entirely possible that 2d12 damage was deemed a lot when you get it and no one paid much attention to whether or not it keeps up.

author: Azaael
body:
I admit, seeing the Venom Monk makes me happy since I can be the Hizoku I always wanted(the clan from King of Fighters, who have the ability to turn their blood poisonous; members include Duo Lon, Ron and Lin if you played the games. The clan names and such were inspired by the Condor Trilogy.) That said, some of them also have the powers of undead like things, so I was able to mess around with Long Death and Shadow to get something going. 
I don't play a lot of 5e, but if I ended up doing so again in a more traditional, non-Eorzea based game I'd totally mess with this if the GM allowed.(The Hizoku clan are not all evil, they're more of a neutral clan with a few members who went bad, but I know in D&D poison is generally looked at as sort of a shady endeavor, even if the character itself doesn't have to be fully evil.) I also quite like the idea behind the Primordial Warlock(I like the ideas of elements being really scary.)

author: La Marche Futilé
body:
I wouldn't even put them in the same class. Frenzy is gonna add 2d6/3d6/4d6 to your damage every single round of every combat, basically. (Yes, you won't always be raging and reckless attacking, but the overwhelming majority of the time you will be.) If you're having fairly standard adventuring days, that's four-round encounters four times per day. In order to even make parity with that, your three uses of doing a Big Sad each have to hit an average of seven enemies, which is incredibly optimistic.
Obviously each will have situations where it is better (Lament is going to overperform in horde encounters, but underperform against bosses, etc) but on the average, Berserker absolutely blows Lament out of the water. Some of the higher-level features have some potential, but I don't know if it's enough to justify putting 6+ levels into barbarian.
Edit: I just noticed that the sleep toxin on the monk doesn't cause the target to wake up on taking damage, only on being shaken awake by an ally. I'm quite sure that's unintentional, but RAW it is actually extremely busted.
